title: Why steam burns worse than boiling water
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why does steam burn more than boiling water?
Is steam hotter than boiling water?

explain.say: Boiling water and steam can both be at 100 degrees Celsius, yet steam gives far worse burns. The difference is hidden energy.

draw.text: Why steam burns worse than boiling water

explain.say: To turn water into steam takes a huge amount of energy, called latent heat. It does not raise the temperature; it goes into pulling the water molecules apart.
When steam lands on your cooler skin it condenses back into water, and all that stored energy is released into your skin at once.
A gram of boiling water cooling to skin temperature gives out about 260 joules. A gram of steam gives about 2,500, nearly ten times as much, which is why steam is so dangerous.

faq.q: Why does steam give a worse burn than boiling water?
faq.a: When steam touches skin it condenses and releases its latent heat on top of the heat from cooling, so it delivers nearly ten times as much energy as the same mass of boiling water.
asks: Why are steam burns so bad?

faq.a: Latent heat is the energy needed to change state, like turning water into steam, without changing the temperature. It is given back when the steam turns into water again.

faq.q: Is the steam from a kettle spout dangerous?
faq.a: Yes. The invisible steam right at the spout is the most dangerous part. The white cloud a little further away is droplets that have already condensed and cooled a bit.

faq.q: What should you do if you get a steam burn?
faq.a: Cool the burn under cool running water for about 20 minutes, remove anything tight nearby, and get an adult or medical help if it is large or blistering.
asks: How do you treat a steam burn?

faq.q: Is steam hotter than boiling water?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Both can be at 100 degrees Celsius. Steam carries much more energy because of its latent heat, so it burns more.

facts: Turning 1 gram of water at 100 degrees Celsius into steam takes about 2,260 joules, more than five times the energy needed to heat it from 0 to 100 degrees.
When steam condenses back into water it releases that same amount of energy.
